PR #20414 should fix this. The root cause: `normalizeMessages()` in `transform.ts` only stripped empty assistant messages when `api.npm === "@ai-sdk/anthropic"`, but GitHub Copilot uses `@ai-sdk/github-copilot`. Meanwhile, the caching transform used a broader name-based check (`api.id.includes("claude")`) that *did* match — so cache metadata got attached to empty assistant messages that should have been removed, causing the prefill error.

The fix extracts a single `isClaudeModel()` helper used at all detection sites, so empty content stripping now also runs for Copilot (and any other non-native SDK path to Claude).

PR #20414 partially addresses this. It fixes root cause #1 (empty/aborted assistant messages surviving) by unifying the Anthropic detection logic — `normalizeMessages()` now strips empty content for all Claude models regardless of SDK package, not just `@ai-sdk/anthropic`.

Root cause #2 (`isLastStep` prefill injection in `prompt.ts` L700-710) is a separate code path that unconditionally appends a trailing assistant message and is **not** addressed by this PR.

I checked commit 4dd866d and it addresses a different issue — it removes the `@ai-sdk/azure` exclusion from the **message-level** `providerOptions` remapping (line ~295 in `transform.ts`). That fix ensures message/part-level options get remapped from a custom provider name to the SDK key.

However, the `reasoningEffort` bug is in `sdkKey()` itself (line 29), which controls the **model-level** `providerOptions` key — the one used when passing options like `reasoningEffort` to `streamText()`. `sdkKey("@ai-sdk/azure")` still returns `"azure"`, but `OpenAIChatLanguageModel` from `@ai-sdk/openai` hardcodes `provider: 'openai'` in `parseProviderOptions`, so it only reads from `providerOptions["openai"]`.

I verified on the latest `dev` branch (with that commit included) that `reasoning_effort` is still missing from the outgoing request body when using an Azure provider with `"options": { "reasoningEffort": "medium" }`.

The fix in #20272 (changing `sdkKey` to return `"openai"` for `@ai-sdk/azure`) is still needed.

@rekram1-node Updated the approach based on your feedback on #20275.

The original fix changed `sdkKey("@ai-sdk/azure")` from `"azure"` to `"openai"`, but that would conflict with your fix in #20326 — `sdkKey` is shared between model-level `providerOptions()` and message-level remapping, and they need different keys (`"openai"` vs `"azure"` respectively).

New approach: keep `sdkKey` returning `"azure"`, and instead have `providerOptions()` pass model options under **both** `"openai"` and `"azure"` for `@ai-sdk/azure`. This works because:
- `OpenAIChatLanguageModel` reads from `providerOptions["openai"]` ✅
- `OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel` reads from `providerOptions["azure"]` first, falls back to `"openai"` ✅
- Message-level remapping still uses `"azure"` via `sdkKey` ✅

Rebased on latest `dev` with #20326 included. Verified that the issue still reproduces on `dev` without this fix.

Let me clarify:

I built a small plugin prototype to test whether workspace bootstrap can be done from plugin code rather than manually through the UI.

What the prototype does successfully:

- creates a workspace via `experimental.workspace.create(...)`
- creates a session bound to that workspace via `session.create({ workspaceID })`
- switches the UI to that session via `tui.selectSession(...)`

What is still not solved:

- the created session still reports the repo root as session.directory
- built-in tools still execute in repo root instead of the workspace directory
- semantic naming is not preserved reliably, because OpenCode still chooses its own workspace name/branch
- the plugin-provided client did not expose the needed workspace APIs directly, so I had to create my own `@opencode-ai/sdk/v2`  client from serverUrl

So the missing capability is not just “GUI switching”, but “plugin-created workspaces becoming the real execution root for the session”.

I’m aware this is still an experimental feature, so I’m sharing this mainly as informative feedback and as a signal of capability interest.

Confirming this on v1.3.13 via a self-hosted LiteLLM proxy, and can add two additional failure modes beyond the Gemini hang.

**1. Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash-preview) — same root cause as described**
Exact behavior from the issue: agent executes the tool call, LiteLLM logs show the response arriving cleanly, then nothing. The proxy's hanging request checker fires every ~2.5 minutes indefinitely. No second dispatch ever happens. The `finish_reason: "stop"` explanation fits perfectly.

**2. Qwen (via OpenRouter) — loop instead of hang**
Rather than stopping, the agent enters a dispatch loop. LiteLLM logs show the same cache key hashed and dispatched twice within the same session after 1–2 tool calls, then the hanging checker fires indefinitely — neither stopping nor progressing. This may be the same `finish_reason` misread causing the loop-continuation logic to re-enter instead of break, depending on how the provider varies its response.

**3. Qwen3-Coder (via NVIDIA) — infinite streaming loop, no stop token**
A harder failure: the model never emits a stop token at all. `streaming_handler.py` streamed the same ~5 bullet points on repeat for 60+ seconds until a forced container restart. After restart, the new container continued receiving the same in-flight stream before the connection dropped. Likely a related but distinct issue — the model may be looping on tool-result processing at the generation level.

All three backends are disabled in config as a workaround.

Still relevant on v1.3.11. We ran into this while building cost analytics for our multi-tenant platform that embeds OpenCode.

Confirmed empirically: title generation, summary titles, and body summaries make LLM calls via `LLM.stream()` but never persist token usage or cost on any message. For title generation specifically (`prompt.ts`), the call uses `provider.getSmallModel()` / the `small_model` config and updates the session title via `sessions.setTitle()` without creating an `AssistantMessage`, so there's no surface to attach usage data to.

For compaction, an `AssistantMessage` is created but tokens are initialized to zero and never populated with actual usage from the LLM call.

As a workaround for the _main prompt_ cost tracking, we accumulate tokens/cost from `step-finish` parts (via `message.part.updated` events) instead of relying on `message.updated` — but that doesn't help with these hidden background costs since they don't emit step-finish parts at all.

Would be great to see this addressed — for BYOK (bring your own key) deployments, accurate cost reporting to end users is critical.

The first typecheck run failed with `../app/node_modules/.ts-dist/src/i18n/ru.d.ts(757,24): error TS1002: Unterminated string literal`. This is in an auto-generated `.d.ts` file inside `node_modules`, not in any source code this PR touches. Re-running the check resolved it, confirming this is an intermittent issue in Bun/tsgo declaration file generation rather than a code problem.

The `e2e (linux/windows)` failures are a known issue affecting all open PRs and are unrelated to this change.
